title: Render Optimization Strategies
description: Profile React rendering, identify bottlenecks, and apply strategies to minimize unnecessary work.

data.text: Before optimizing, you need data. React DevTools Profiler records component renders and shows how long each render takes. It also highlights why components re-rendered and which props changed.

data.title: Recording a Profile
data.content: Open React DevTools, go to the Profiler tab, and click Record. Interact with your app, then stop recording. The flame graph shows render durations.

data.title: Use Production Builds for Accurate Metrics
data.text: Development builds add extra overhead. Always measure performance in a production build to get realistic numbers.
The Profiler shows which components re-rendered and why. Look for patterns such as a parent re-rendering many children, or components re-rendering when their props have not meaningfully changed.

data.caption: Diagnosing render paths
data.definition:
graph TD
    A[Profiler Trace] --> B{Render Time > 16ms?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Find Hot Component]
    B -->|No| D[Performance Acceptable]
    C --> E{Props Actually Changed?}
    E -->|No| F[Add React.memo]
    E -->|Yes| G[Optimize Computation or Split State]

data.text: One of the most effective ways to reduce re-renders is to restructure your component tree. If only a small part of a component needs dynamic data, lift that part into a separate component so the rest of the UI is stable.

data.title: Extracting Dynamic Content
data.content: Before: the entire list re-renders when count changes. After: only the counter re-renders.

data.text: State colocation means keeping state as close as possible to where it is used. Global or lifted state forces unrelated components to re-render. By colocating state, only the components that truly need it subscribe to updates.

data.title: State Colocation Strategies
items: Move state into the component that consumes it
Use local state for UI-only concerns like toggles and inputs
Avoid lifting state to the top of the tree for one-off interactions
Consider component composition before context or global stores

data.text: Inline objects and arrow functions in JSX create new references on every render. When these are passed to memoized children, they break memoization. Use useMemo and useCallback to stabilize references.

data.title: Avoiding Prop Drift
data.content: Use useMemo and useCallback to keep prop references stable across renders.

data.text: React 18+ automatically batches state updates, even inside promises and event handlers. This reduces the number of renders and improves perceived performance. Use startTransition to mark non-urgent updates as interruptible.

data.title: Using startTransition
data.content: Mark heavy UI updates as transitions so React can prioritize urgent input.

cards.title: React.memo
cards.description: Prevents re-renders when props are shallowly equal.

cards.title: useMemo / useCallback
cards.description: Stabilizes values and function references between renders.

cards.title: Component Splitting
cards.description: Moves dynamic parts into isolated components.

cards.title: Transitions
cards.description: Marks updates as non-urgent for better responsiveness.

items.text: Profile with React DevTools before optimizing
items.hint: Find the actual bottleneck, do not guess

items.text: Memoize props passed to expensive children
Colocate state near where it is used

items.hint: Keep the UI responsive during heavy work
Ensure your change actually reduced render time

data.title: Practice: Profile and Optimize a Slow Component
data.description: Find a slow-rendering component in your app and apply optimization strategies until its render time drops below the 16ms frame budget.
steps: Open React DevTools Profiler and record a problematic interaction
Identify the component with the longest render time
Check if it receives new props despite unchanged data
Apply React.memo if props are stable
Colocate dynamic state into a child component
Record again and verify render time improved
data.expectedOutcome: The targeted component renders consistently under 16ms with stable props and isolated state.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Profile first using React DevTools to find real bottlenecks
Use composition to isolate dynamic parts of the UI
Colocate state to reduce unnecessary subscribers
Stabilize prop references with useMemo and useCallback
Use React 18 transitions to keep the UI responsive during heavy updates
